notes: One of the three records a round-55 agent returned on the audit-office route. FIJI was refused: the agent's own summary says the committee's report is largely commendatory, and it is a statutory review of annual reports with no adverse finding, no summons and no demand on the bank. The same agent ruled out Namibia because the governor's appearance was 'in line with the statutory reporting requirements' of the Bank of Namibia Act, and ruled out Solomon Islands for consistency with that; filing Fiji would contradict both. Routine oversight is not the state acting against the bank -- that is the Finland and Luxembourg test, no adversary and nothing to count. MYANMAR was refused for the third time across three rounds: round 52 settled that the junta court's secret-trial conviction of Bo Bo Nge stays on the moves layer only, because the corruption row is built from audits, inquiries and open courts and a military government's secret-trial conviction set beside those would read as evidence that the official was corrupt rather than as evidence of what the state did to the bank. It is already on the moves layer and in the Myanmar paragraph. PAKISTAN is the one kept, and it matters out of proportion to one record: Pakistan was the last place on the map holding only uncounted 'other' events, so it rendered blank on the moves layer by design. This gives it a counted episode.

records.kind: public accounts committee directs state audit of the central bank
records.summary: Pakistan's National Assembly Public Accounts Committee, chaired by MNA Noor Alam Khan, directed the Auditor General to conduct an audit of the State Bank of Pakistan over the disbursement of about Rs1,145 billion in TERF concessional loans, after a preliminary report from NAB and the Auditor General, and directed an inquiry into whether the loans were disbursed on merit.
records.source_title: PAC Directs Auditor General to Conduct Audit of State Bank Over TERF Loans
